hypotheses.observation: The authentic Megatron MLP path reaches the fused activation boundary, while the measured model-level scope fraction is 0.015571342909175317 and paired fraction is 0.041956971532107534.
hypotheses.mechanism: Additional fusion around the SwiGLU activation boundary could reduce intermediate tensor materialization and kernel-launch overhead.
hypotheses.transformation: Evaluate a boundary-preserving fused execution strategy that combines adjacent SwiGLU elementwise operations and minimizes intermediate reads and writes.
preconditions: The adjacent operations are compatible with the existing authentic fused activation boundary.
Numerical behavior and supported tensor shapes remain acceptable.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Potential reduction in activation-boundary memory traffic and launch overhead; model-level benefit is expected to be bounded by the measured scope fraction.
risks: More aggressive fusion may increase register usage.
Fusion may reduce applicability across shapes or hardware configurations.
The measured scope fraction may limit end-to-end impact.
unknowns: The boundary kernel breakdown is unknown.
The contribution of launch overhead versus memory traffic is unknown.
Register pressure after fusion is unknown.
required_evidence: Kernel-level timing breakdown for the SwiGLU boundary.
Memory traffic and launch-count comparison before and after the transformation.

hypotheses.observation: Instrumentation overhead is measured at 3.45 percent of model performance, and the model-level operator scope fraction is 0.015571342909175317.
hypotheses.mechanism: Reducing instrumentation and dispatch overhead on the measured SwiGLU path may improve the fidelity and efficiency of the boundary execution.
hypotheses.transformation: Use a lower-overhead measurement and dispatch path localized to the authentic fused activation boundary, while retaining equivalent observability.
preconditions: The measurement path can be localized without changing the authentic execution path.
The resulting measurements remain sufficient to attribute boundary performance.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Potentially lower profiling perturbation and reduced non-compute overhead around the boundary; any end-to-end gain is expected to be limited by the model-level scope fraction.
risks: Reduced instrumentation may hide relevant kernel behavior.
Changes to measurement placement can make comparisons less reliable.
Dispatch overhead may be negligible relative to kernel execution.
unknowns: The fraction of the 3.45 percent overhead attributable specifically to SwiGLU is unknown.
The boundary kernel breakdown is unknown.
The current number and cost of boundary launches are unknown.
required_evidence: Kernel launch count and dispatch-time breakdown.
A comparison with equivalent measurement coverage and no extra instrumentation.

hypotheses.observation: Register pressure is explicitly unknown, and the measured layer, block, and model scope fractions are 0.017922390002669215, 0.017372186944844988, and 0.015571342909175317 respectively.
hypotheses.mechanism: The best transformation may be constrained by the occupancy tradeoff between more fusion and lower register pressure.
hypotheses.transformation: Tune the fusion boundary and intermediate representation to balance eliminated memory traffic against register consumption and occupancy.
preconditions: Register usage and occupancy can be measured for candidate boundary organizations.
The authentic fused activation path remains intact.
hypotheses.expected_effect: Potential improvement when reduced memory traffic outweighs occupancy loss; possible regression if additional fusion causes register spilling or materially lowers occupancy.
risks: Register spilling can increase local-memory traffic.
Lower occupancy can offset or exceed savings from fewer intermediates.
The small operator scope may make any local gain difficult to observe at model level.
unknowns: Occupancy and spilling behavior are unknown.
The boundary kernel time distribution is unknown.
required_evidence: Registers per thread, occupancy, and spill metrics.
Kernel-level timing for multiple fusion-boundary organizations.
End-to-end measurements with the same workload and instrumentation conditions.
